doc.title: Tom Albert and Milton "Mooney" Martin Interview, 1964-12-21

chapter: Algiers places, ball games and Frankie Duson
title: Frankie Duson's job: not a barber, only music
summary: Russell asks whether Frankie Duson had another job. Tom and Martin say his father was a barber but Frankie never was, and as far as they know he did nothing but music.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Can you remember anything more about Deucin over across the river, Mooney? Deucin? Did he have any other job or just music?
I never knew about Deucin no way. I knew he knew he was no way. His father had a barber shop. That's right. His father, oh, that's right. Yeah, old man Deucin. His father had a barber shop. Yeah.
I thought maybe somebody told me he was a barber too, but he wasn't a barber.
Who was that, Frankie? Yeah. No, I never knew Frankie Deucin. He never did a barber. He never did a barber.
He never did a barber. I knew him since I was there. I never knew him to have a job.
I believe Fess told me he was a good ball player. Do you remember? Did he play baseball much?
I don't know him to play baseball.
